label: fiction
title: The Lobby Frame
setting: The court sits in the present-day fictional city of Aster Reach. Shortly after one o’clock in the morning, an alarm drew patrol officer Dax Mere into the municipal evidence archive. He met an unidentified person inside and died before help arrived. Lena Voss, the technician responsible for the archive alarm, now stands accused of murdering an on-duty police officer.
charge: murder of an on-duty police officer
elements: The accused caused the on-duty officer’s death.
The accused intended to kill or cause really serious injury.
The killing was not legally justified or excused.
hook: A genuine lobby frame shows Lena crossing the archive beneath a clock reading 1:31. Dax was already dead by then—or so the display suggests. Before deciding what that image proves, the jury must learn which systems kept central time, what happened when the archive recorder restarted, and where Lena travelled next.

accused.human: Lena Voss, 38, has maintained municipal alarm systems for eleven years. Her work involves overnight callouts, shared maintenance credentials, and confidential access cards. Weeks before Dax’s death, a supervisor warned her for failing to document repairs. She says professional embarrassment explains her hidden visit and first false account, but not the killing.
accused.if_guilty: If convicted, sentencing would be decided separately by the judge. The jury’s task is limited to deciding whether the prosecution proved the charge.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: Dax Mere answered an alarm as part of his ordinary duty and was deliberately killed inside the archive. Lena had secretly entered with her service card, concealed an unauthorised repair, and first told investigators she stayed home. A genuine lobby frame shows her there. She also knew the system and could use the shared credential that disabled clock synchronisation. You will hear the transit and restart evidence too. The prosecution says the records must be weighed together, including their limits, before you decide whether her deception surrounded a repair or a murder.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: Lena’s lie made her a proper suspect, and the defence will not excuse it. But a hidden repair is not proof of homicide. The systems in this case did not all keep the same time. Sela Rune will explain how the original files were obtained, preserved, and checked; what the archive recorded when it restarted; and how a centrally timed gate and continuous carriage video trace Lena’s journey. The defence says those independent records place her away before Dax entered, while his final recording identifies nobody.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: Lena’s concealed entry, false account, technical access, and knowledge that alarm responders might attend are not trivial. The transit gate records a pass, not its carrier, and the shared credential records no individual user. Yet you must also confront the continuous carriage video and the automatic restart entry. The prosecution bears the burden on identity as well as the agreed homicide and intent. If you accept the corrected sequence as reliable and it leaves you unsure Lena met Dax, suspicion—even serious suspicion—cannot lawfully complete the case.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: The chronology is now complete. The authenticated restart entry converts the displayed lobby time to a departure before Dax arrived. Three minutes later, a centrally timed gate recorded Lena’s pass; continuous video then shows her board, remain aboard throughout the fatal window, and leave across the city. Her lie concerned an unauthorised repair and damaged her credibility. It did not alter the automatic records, identify the shadowed person on Dax’s camera, or prove Lena caused his death beyond reasonable doubt.

epilogue: After the proceedings, the city replaced the archive recorder and required independent clock checks for every serious investigation. Dax Mere’s sister kept pressing for answers about the unidentified person on his final recording. Lena Voss left overnight alarm work while the employment inquiry examined her hidden repair. The two families continued living with different parts of the same unresolved night.

beats.speaker: w1

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: How well did you know Dax Mere?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: We partnered for eighteen months. He was careful and kind, checked my reports without making me feel small, and called his sister after every night shift.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: What did an archive alarm usually require?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: The first officer checked the entrance, announced their presence, and waited if anything looked wrong. Dax didn’t treat routine calls casually.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: What happened on his final call?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: Dispatch sent him at 1:16. His body camera connected at 1:18. I heard him ask someone to stop, then the sound broke up. I followed when he didn’t answer.

beats.text: How well did you know Dax Mere? We partnered for eighteen months. He was careful and kind, checked my reports without making me feel small, and called his sister after every night shift. What did an archive alarm usually require? The first officer checked the entrance, announced their presence, and waited if anything looked wrong. Dax didn’t treat routine calls casually. What happened on his final call? Dispatch sent him at 1:16. His body camera connected at 1:18. I heard him ask someone to stop, then the sound broke up. I followed when he didn’t answer.
beats.reveal_note: Eren’s first-hand account established when Dax began the call and treated him as a person, but it did not identify who attacked him.

beats.speaker: judge
beats.text: The parties agree that a qualified forensic physician examined Dax and reviewed the emergency records. Dax died between 1:19 and 1:24 from deliberate force by another person. Those findings exclude accident, natural illness, and self-infliction. They also prove the attacker intended to kill or cause really serious injury and acted without lawful justification. In legal terms, causation, murderous intent, and absence of justification are agreed. The prosecution must still prove the remaining element: that Lena was the attacker.
beats.reveal_note: The agreed medical evidence proved an unlawful intentional homicide within a defined window. It was deliberately neutral about who committed it.

beats.speaker: pc
beats.text: The city camera custodian exported the original lobby recording in an investigator’s presence, retained the source drive, and verified that the export matched the retained original. The unedited frame displays 1:31 and clearly shows Lena crossing the lobby in her work coat. The file and face are authentic. Matching the file does not prove that the recorder’s displayed clock was accurate.
beats.reveal_note: The authenticated frame proved Lena’s identity, but not its real capture time. The later restart evidence changed 1:31 to 1:13.

beats.speaker: w1

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: The body-camera figure never shows a face, does it?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: No. I wish it did, but the face stays in shadow.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: And you cannot identify the voice as Lena’s?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: I can’t. It’s brief and distorted.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Dax never says Lena’s name or describes the person?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: No. The recording proves he met someone inside during the fatal window. It doesn’t tell me who that person was, and I won’t pretend it does.

beats.text: The body-camera figure never shows a face, does it? No. I wish it did, but the face stays in shadow. And you cannot identify the voice as Lena’s? I can’t. It’s brief and distorted. Dax never says Lena’s name or describes the person? No. The recording proves he met someone inside during the fatal window. It doesn’t tell me who that person was, and I won’t pretend it does.
beats.reveal_note: Eren resisted overstating the fatal recording. It established an encounter but supplied no usable identification.

beats.speaker: pc
beats.text: The access-system custodian produced the original server register and verified its audit signature. Lena’s service card opened the archive at 12:47. No later entry used it, although lobby exits needed no card. Lena omitted the visit and first said she stayed home. Dax’s signed call note says he planned to ask her about the unexplained access. The register proves use of her card at 12:47, not how long she remained or who carried it.
beats.reveal_note: The authenticated register and Lena’s lie established a concealed visit. They did not extend that visit into the medical window.

beats.speaker: w2

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: What transit material did you examine?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: The transit custodian supplied the original East Quay gate log, platform video, and continuous carriage video. I checked each signed export against the retained source.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: How did you test their clocks?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: The gate and both cameras synchronised with the city’s central time service. Their daily checks were within one second, with no reset or jump that night.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: What journey do they record?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: Lena’s pass opened the gate at 1:16. Video shows her board at 1:18 and remain visible until West Crossing at 1:29. Even the nearest return route to the archive takes ten minutes.

beats.text: What transit material did you examine? The transit custodian supplied the original East Quay gate log, platform video, and continuous carriage video. I checked each signed export against the retained source. How did you test their clocks? The gate and both cameras synchronised with the city’s central time service. Their daily checks were within one second, with no reset or jump that night. What journey do they record? Lena’s pass opened the gate at 1:16. Video shows her board at 1:18 and remain visible until West Crossing at 1:29. Even the nearest return route to the archive takes ten minutes.
beats.reveal_note: The examiner established provenance, integrity, identity, and independent central timing for the two transit records.

beats.speaker: w2

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: How did you test the archive recorder itself?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: I imaged its original drive in an investigator’s presence. We recorded the drive ID, sealed the drive, and verified that my working copy still matched the lobby export.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Why could its displayed time differ from central time?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: The recorder restarted after a power interruption. Its automatic system log says synchronisation was disabled, so at 10:04 it loaded a clock eighteen minutes fast.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: What did its restart record show?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: Every later frame retained that fixed difference. The displayed 1:31 lobby frame was captured at 1:13 central time. The restart entry was written automatically, hours before Lena became a suspect.

Every later frame retained that fixed difference. The displayed 1:31 lobby frame was captured at 1:13 central time. The restart entry was written automatically, hours before Lena became a suspect.
beats.reveal_note: The examiner authenticated the original drive, its custody, and the automatic restart entry before explaining the exact correction.

beats.speaker: w2

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: The gate log alone does not identify who carried Lena’s pass?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: That’s correct. The platform and carriage video identify her from 1:18 onward.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: And the restart entry does not name who disabled synchronization?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: No. A shared maintenance credential disabled it at 9:52; four technicians, including Lena, could use that credential.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: So your records cannot tell us why the clock was changed?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: They can’t identify purpose or user. They do show the change occurred before Lena’s 12:47 entry, and the automatic restart entry fixes the amount of error.

So your records cannot tell us why the clock was changed? They can’t identify purpose or user. They do show the change occurred before Lena’s 12:47 entry, and the automatic restart entry fixes the amount of error.
beats.reveal_note: The prosecution exposed real limitations and Lena’s access to a shared credential. The examiner also preserved the independent carriage identification and the restart entry’s timing.

beats.speaker: acc

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: What mistake had you made at the archive?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: I’d rushed an alarm repair and never opened the required work ticket. After my earlier warning, I panicked about losing trusted callout work.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Why did you return that night?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: I thought I could finish the repair and document it the next morning. That was dishonest and stupid, but I didn’t expect Dax or anyone else.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: What do you remember about leaving?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: I didn’t check the lobby clock. I locked my tools, walked quickly to East Quay, used my pass, and boarded the waiting carriage. I stayed aboard to West Crossing.

beats.text: What mistake had you made at the archive? I’d rushed an alarm repair and never opened the required work ticket. After my earlier warning, I panicked about losing trusted callout work. Why did you return that night? I thought I could finish the repair and document it the next morning. That was dishonest and stupid, but I didn’t expect Dax or anyone else. What do you remember about leaving? I didn’t check the lobby clock. I locked my tools, walked quickly to East Quay, used my pass, and boarded the waiting carriage. I stayed aboard to West Crossing.
beats.reveal_note: Lena gave a human explanation rather than reciting the records. Her account still required independent support, which the jury had already heard.

beats.speaker: acc

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: You first told investigators you had stayed home?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: Yes. I lied because I was ashamed and afraid of another warning. I corrected it when they showed me the access record.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: You could use the shared maintenance credential?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: For alarm work, yes, like three other technicians.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: And you knew an alarm could bring a patrol officer?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: Of course. I believed the repair had cleared it. I didn’t disable the clock, I didn’t attack Dax, and I was already on the carriage when he arrived.

beats.text: You first told investigators you had stayed home? Yes. I lied because I was ashamed and afraid of another warning. I corrected it when they showed me the access record. You could use the shared maintenance credential? For alarm work, yes, like three other technicians. And you knew an alarm could bring a patrol officer? Of course. I believed the repair had cleared it. I didn’t disable the clock, I didn’t attack Dax, and I was already on the carriage when he arrived.
beats.reveal_note: The cross-examination secured two damaging admissions—Lena lied and had credential access—while leaving both the shared access and independent timeline intact.

beats.speaker: judge
beats.text: For orientation, the parties agree that every time in this chronology uses central time after the recorder correction. At 9:52, a shared credential disabled synchronisation. At 10:04, the recorder restarted eighteen minutes fast. Lena’s card entered at 12:47; the corrected lobby frame shows her leave at 1:13. Her pass opened East Quay gate at 1:16, and video shows her aboard from 1:18 until 1:29. Dax’s camera connected at 1:18; the fatal encounter occurred between 1:19 and 1:24. The sequence does not identify the credential user or explain Lena’s lie.
beats.reveal_note: The agreed central-time chronology lets first-time jurors compare every event without silently mixing the recorder display with verified time.

beats.speaker: judge
beats.text: The charge has three elements. First, the prosecution must prove Lena caused Dax’s death. Because everyone agrees another person deliberately killed him, that element turns on identity: was Lena that person? Second, the attacker must have intended to kill or cause really serious injury. Third, the killing must lack lawful justification or excuse. Intent and absence of justification are agreed, but that agreement cannot prove identity. The prosecution bears the burden throughout. Lena does not have to identify the attacker, prove her journey, or explain every lie. A false account may damage credibility or support an inference, but it cannot replace proof of an element. Circumstantial evidence may be sufficient; assess what each record proves and what it cannot prove. If, after considering all the evidence, you are not sure the prosecution proved every element beyond reasonable doubt, your verdict must be Not Guilty. Use only evidence heard in court and do not research the case.
beats.reveal_note: The direction separates the agreed homicide from disputed identity and states the criminal standard without converting any imaginable doubt into reasonable doubt.

twist: The authors’ reference resolution is Not Guilty. The authenticated restart entry maps the lobby frame to 1:13, before Dax arrived, and the centrally timed carriage image then identifies Lena away during the fatal window. The strongest prosecution interpretation is that her hidden visit, lie, and access to the shared credential show a planned deception. Those facts are probative, but they do not overcome the verified sequence or identify her in the fatal encounter.

jurors.label: Juror 2 — Anya
jurors.persona: Starts with the vivid lobby image, then asks whether its timestamp deserves the same confidence.

agree: I saw Lena’s face and stopped there. Doesn’t that image still matter?
pushback: Wait—which clock are we trusting, and why?
concede: All right, the carriage image changes it. That clock was independently checked.
burden_drift: She lied first. Why shouldn’t she have to fill every missing minute?
burden_correct: No, that’s backwards. Her lie is evidence, but the prosecution still has to identify Dax’s attacker.
final: I’m not sure Lena was there for the fatal encounter.

jurors.label: Juror 3 — Bram
jurors.persona: Keeps separating an authenticated file from the inference someone wants drawn from it.

agree: The access register proves the secret visit. I don’t think we can minimise that.
pushback: But 12:47 isn’t 1:20. What bridges that gap?
concede: The restart entry gives us a measured correction, not a guess.
burden_drift: I keep wanting a complete account from Lena because the work ticket is missing.
burden_correct: The records still have to satisfy the prosecution’s burden; suspicion can’t complete them.
final: The reliable timestamps don’t place Lena with Dax.

jurors.label: Juror 4 — Cora
jurors.persona: Keeps returning the room to disputed identity when strong feelings pull it toward the agreed homicide.

agree: The defence timeline is supported by records created before anyone was accused.
pushback: Who can identify Lena in Dax’s final recording? Nobody has.
concede: I accept the lie was serious. I don’t accept that it identifies a murderer.
burden_drift: The concealment is tempting us to demand that Lena prove innocence.
burden_correct: The judge told us what to ask: are we sure the prosecution proved every element?
final: I’m holding out because identity hasn’t been proved.

jurors.label: Juror 5 — Dev
jurors.persona: Initially trusts the simple camera story, but changes position when the underlying records are tested.

agree: The camera is genuine. That’s why I started on Guilty.
pushback: Genuine picture, wrong time. Why are we treating those as the same thing?
concede: Eighteen minutes resolves the conflict without inventing a missing event.
burden_drift: Part of me still wants Lena to solve this because she caused the repair mess.
burden_correct: A hidden repair isn’t a killing. We can’t blur them together.
final: I changed my mind once the real capture time was proved.

jurors.label: Juror 6 — Pax
jurors.persona: Organises the discussion by proposition and stops the room from treating agreed homicide as agreed identity.

agree: Let’s mark it clearly: Lena entered, hid the visit, and lied.
pushback: Now the next question: what proves she stayed for Dax’s arrival?
concede: Once 1:31 becomes 1:13, the records fit together.
burden_drift: We’re starting to make Lena’s lie carry a duty to prove innocence.
burden_correct: Identity is still the prosecution’s element. Has it been proved beyond reasonable doubt?
final: The homicide is agreed. Lena’s identity as the attacker isn’t.

jurors.label: Juror 7 — Fia
jurors.persona: Speaks before settling, then corrects herself aloud when another juror exposes a missing step.

agree: I’ll be honest: face plus 1:31 looked decisive to me.
pushback: Hold on. The picture can be true while the printed time is wrong.
concede: Yes, I see it now—the restart entry makes the error concrete.
burden_drift: Because Lena hid the repair, I keep wanting her to remove every doubt.
burden_correct: That isn’t her job. The prosecution has to prove the identity element.
final: I was anchored by the first image, and I’ve changed my view.

jurors.label: Juror 8 — Garen
jurors.persona: Tests whether independent evidence confirms the same proposition and is willing to reverse an early position.

agree: The lobby frame is authentic, and I initially treated that as proof of guilt.
pushback: But what authenticated the recorder’s clock? Not the image authenticity alone.
concede: The independent sources show my first reading was wrong.
burden_drift: Lena’s dishonesty makes an unsupported inference feel safer than it is.
burden_correct: The prosecution must prove the fatal encounter, not merely an earlier visit.
final: The verified sequence puts Lena away before Dax met the attacker.

jurors.label: Juror 9 — Hale
jurors.persona: Listens for the limit in each witness’s answer and challenges anyone who quietly goes beyond it.

agree: Eren was careful: Dax met someone, but the recording identifies nobody.
pushback: Are we joining an earlier clear face to a later shadow and calling them one person?
concede: Lena’s lie damages her. The transit records still support why she said she left.
burden_drift: Dax’s death is terrible, and that can make unexplained conduct feel like guilt.
burden_correct: The seriousness of the charge makes accurate identification more important, not less.
final: I can’t identify Lena as Dax’s attacker.

jurors.label: Juror 10 — Iri
jurors.persona: Reacts strongly to Lena’s lie and has to be challenged when suspicion starts shifting the burden.

agree: Dax planned to question Lena. That gives the lie a sharper edge.
pushback: Still, a workplace cover-up doesn’t identify a murderer.
concede: I can’t brush aside a face on a centrally timed carriage.
burden_drift: Lena lied first, so I want her to tell us who else was inside.
burden_correct: No—that puts it on her. The prosecution has to prove Lena was the attacker.
final: I dislike what she did, but I’m not sure she committed murder.

jurors.label: Juror 11 — Joss
jurors.persona: Voices uncertainty as the sequence develops and corrects his own shorthand when it stops fitting.

agree: I followed the simple story: camera means she left afterward.
pushback: But that story uses the displayed time. What happens when it’s corrected?
concede: The gate, carriage, and restart entry now make one sequence for me.
burden_drift: I keep thinking Lena should fill the gap because she was dishonest.
burden_correct: Actually, the gap belongs to the prosecution’s case, doesn’t it?
final: The reliable sequence leaves Lena away from the fatal encounter.

jurors.label: Juror 12 — Kemi
jurors.persona: Insists on stating the strongest argument for each side before deciding what remains unproved.

agree: The restart and transit records support one another without sharing a clock.
pushback: The prosecution’s best point is concealment. Which record carries it into the fatal window?
concede: I agree Lena’s denial made her a proper suspect and deserved investigation.
burden_drift: It’s easy to ask Lena for the answer because Dax’s attacker remains unknown.
burden_correct: An unknown attacker doesn’t reduce the prosecution’s burden.
final: The evidence proves a hidden visit, not the charged murder.
